title: Where the Harlem Grill was in Houston
summary: Cobb locates the Harlem Grill on West Dallas near Heiner, a main Houston dance spot until the Eldorado opened in 1937.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: What did you call it? The Bar and Grill you played at?
It was in the Fogwater area on West [Dallas] and Hiener; that was one of the main spots during those days in the thirties.
So that was a dance bar, was it?

That was it, until the Eldorado came out in '37. But like in '34, and I would tell you I was making $34 a week for 6 days a week there as a schoolboy. All the little girls bet me for a nickel block of ice cream because I had some money in my pocket.
